confidence_notes: I based the food and drink anchors on one cost-of-living search. Its crowd-sourced figures from MyLifeElsewhere gave about PLN 41.5 for an inexpensive meal, PLN 13.5 for a domestic beer and PLN 14 for a cappuccino. Lower guide-style ranges on the CostLiving sites look outdated, so I gave them little weight. I didn't find direct figures for the mid-range meal for two, cocktails or wine. I estimated those from beer prices and general Polish price levels, so they're less certain. The accommodation anchors come from general knowledge only, not from searches or live listings. They allow for the July summer peak and for trade fairs in Poznań, which can push hotel rates up. The FX rate is the RBA 4pm observation for 18 November 2026 as reported in the search result, and it's the latest rate available on the generation date. I couldn't open the RBA page directly to confirm it.
comparable_city_reasoning: Prices should be similar to Wrocław and Gdańsk and slightly below Kraków and Warsaw. Poznań is a mid-sized Polish city with a large student population and many business visitors.
